buildSourceNote: Build 138 carries v1.1.0-rc.14. The owner reported that the developer login 'needs every access'. The premise was wrong, and checking it found two real defects. The signed-in tab was sayeed_dp (user 21, gm_service), NOT the developer login - the only ACTIVE developer account is wmsdmworkshop@gmail.com (user 48); the older 'developer' account (user 30) is deactivated. Both the GM and the developer are named Sayeed, which is how the two get confused; the loaded account was confirmed by reading dwip_auth_user from localStorage rather than assuming. DEFECT 1 - AND THE FIRST VERSION OF THIS NOTE WAS WRONG, CORRECTED 2026-09-16 AFTER VERIFYING THE DEPLOYED BUNDLE: the excludedTabs list was written out TWICE with different behaviour - the redirect guard exempted admin, developer, dealer_principal, gm_service and workshop_manager while the sidebar filter exempted nobody - and both call sites now share RC1_EXCLUDED_TABS and RC1_TAB_EXEMPT_ROLES through isRc1TabHidden(), so the two cannot diverge again. BUT THE rc1 PROFILE IS INERT IN PRODUCTION, so that filter has never removed anything there. .dockerignore AND .gcloudignore both carry '.env' and '.env.*', and .env.rc1 - the only file that sets VITE_WORKFORCE_PROFILE=rc1 - is ALSO gitignored, so it never reaches the Cloud Build upload or the Docker context. 'vite build --mode rc1' consequently loads no env file, VITE_WORKFORCE_PROFILE is undefined, the comparison folds to false, and the whole guard is eliminated as dead code. PROVED AGAINST THE LIVE BUNDLE, not inferred: 'rc1' appears ZERO times in /assets/index-dw5hAiI8.js, the excluded-tabs array literal is absent, and no rc1 branch survives - esbuild removed it. THE PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE IS THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT THIS NOTE INITIALLY RECORDED: developer has NOT been losing six tabs, because it already sees all of ROLE_TABS.developer, and the owner's 'needs every access' report must have another cause - most likely working from sayeed_dp (gm_service), whose tab set is genuinely smaller. The dedup shipped in rc.14 is therefore correct hygiene but a NO-OP in production. WHETHER TO ACTUALLY ENABLE rc1 IS AN OPEN OWNER DECISION: switching it on would HIDE six tabs in production, the opposite of what was asked for, so it was deliberately left alone rather than fixed silently. DEFECT 2, AND THIS ONE WAS MINE: rc.13 added 'reception' to GATE_OUT_SECURITY_ROLES but gave reception no way to use it. The only caller of POST /api/gate-out/gate-out in the entire repository is SecurityWorkspace.tsx:63, which renders only on activeTab === security-workspace, and ROLE_TABS.reception held just vehicle-lookup and gate-entry. MyWorkspace.tsx has ZERO gate or security references, so there was no fallback path either. Reception held the authority and had nowhere to use it. security-workspace is now in reception's list - added to reception ONLY, not receptionist, because granting the tab to a role the API does not authorise creates the inverse defect, a button that 403s; and security-workspace is absent from TAB_MODULE_MAPPING, so isTabPermitted passes it through. Also recorded while checking: security_agent and gate_personnel do NOT have that tab either - only admin, developer, workshop_manager, service_manager, gm_service and dealer_principal do - so gate-out has in practice been worked by admin and the GM, not by security. NOT CHANGED and flagged for the owner: service_manager, supervisor and floor_supervisor also have breakdown spliced in by the ROLE_TABS loop and are not in RC1_TAB_EXEMPT_ROLES, so they still lose it in production; widening that list is a policy decision about who sees Breakdowns in production. See docs/CHANGELOG.md.

Revision chain: 00242-j6h (rc.11) -> 00243-z7w (rc.12) -> 00244-st5 (rc.13) -> 00245-48s (rc.14). rc.13 changed the API gate only, so on its own it granted reception an authority it could not exercise; rc.14 is the nav half that makes it usable, and THAT half IS verified live - the served bundle contains reception with vehicle-lookup, gate-entry AND security-workspace, while receptionist correctly does not. STILL OPEN, PRODUCTION-WIDE, FOUND WHILE VERIFYING rc.14: the rc1 workforce profile never applies. .dockerignore and .gcloudignore both exclude '.env' and '.env.*', and .env.rc1 is gitignored as well, so VITE_WORKFORCE_PROFILE is undefined at build time in Cloud Build. Every 'import.meta.env.VITE_WORKFORCE_PROFILE === rc1' check in the codebase is therefore permanently false in production - the App.tsx tab guard AND AttendanceShiftLog.tsx. Confirmed against the live bundle: zero occurrences of 'rc1', zero of 'dev', and the excluded-tabs array literal absent. Net effect today is permissive (nothing is hidden), so it is NOT an outage - but it means the production-hardening configuration is documentation rather than behaviour. Needs an OWNER DECISION: either set VITE_WORKFORCE_PROFILE via a Docker ARG/ENV or build arg so it survives the context exclusion, or accept that rc1 is inert and delete the dead checks. `.env.*` must stay dockerignored otherwise - it is the right instinct, and .env.rc1 happens to carry no secret, which is the ONLY reason a build flag cannot ride along with it.
